In 2026, a proposal for reducing costs to homeowners was floated: Increasing the mortgage duration from the typical 30 years to 50 years or more will reduce the monthly payment. @fig-seal-form-glasses shows two graphs of the `monthly_payment()` function.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-seal-form-glasses
#| fig-cap: "Monthly mortgage payment for a principal of $200,000."
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-subcap: 
#| - "at 7% interest."
#| - "at 30 years duration"

slice_plot(QRA::monthly_payment(200000, 7, duration) ~ duration, domain(duration=10:100)) |>
gf_theme(theme_minimal(base_size = 12)) |>
gf_labs(x = "Duration (years)", y = "Monthly Payment ($)") |>
gf_lims(y=c(0, NA))

slice_plot(QRA::monthly_payment(200000, rate, 30) ~ rate, domain(rate=2:15)) |>
gf_theme(theme_minimal(base_size = 12)) |>
gf_labs(x = "Interest rate (%)", y = "Monthly Payment ($)") |>
gf_lims(y=c(0, NA))
```

How can one function, `monthly_payment()` have two different graphs? 

`r devoirs::devoirs_text("sfg-1-kr3s")`

Which of the two panels---(a) or (b)---gives insight into the suggested long-duration policy? 

`r devoirs::devoirs_text("sfg-2-kr3s")`
:::
